key_insight: A deep-learning system trained on 45,139 prenatal ultrasound images from 9,215 fetuses across 22 hospitals can accurately detect fetal orofacial clefts, enabling earlier and more consistent prenatal diagnosis than is possible with limited specialist availability.
problem_solved: Addresses the difficulty of reliable prenatal detection of orofacial clefts caused by scarce experienced sonographers and the relative rarity of the condition, which limits early intervention and consistent screening.
method: Curated a multi-center dataset (45,139 ultrasound images from 9,215 fetuses across 22 hospitals) to capture diverse imaging conditions and patient populations.
Trained a convolutional neural network–based diagnostic model (with localization/attention maps for explainability) to classify and localize orofacial clefts on standard prenatal ultrasound views.
Validated performance across sites and integrated interpretability outputs to support clinical review and use in medical education/training.
impact: Provides a scalable, generalizable AI tool that can improve prenatal screening accuracy, reduce dependence on rare specialist expertise, and serve as an educational aid for clinicians and sonographers; useful reference for ML practitioners focused on multi-site medical imaging, robustness, and explainability.
visual_elements: World/region map or hospital network graphic showing 22-hospital multi-center dataset coverage and sample counts
Model pipeline diagram: input ultrasound → CNN feature extraction → classifier + attention heatmap → diagnosis
Before/after ultrasound examples: original image alongside model heatmap highlighting cleft localization
Performance chart (ROC/precision-recall) and a bar showing cross-site generalization / sensitivity & specificity
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence for Detecting Fetal Orofacial Clefts and Advancing Medical Education
paper_authors: Yuanji Zhang, Yuhao Huang, Haoran Dou, Xiliang Zhu, Chen Ling
